claims: The Artemis 2 mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis 2 mission had a four-person crew.
The Artemis 2 crew completed a 10-day mission.
The Artemis 2 mission marked the first crewed return to Earth from the moon in over 50 years.
The Artemis 2 splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
The recovery vessel for the Artemis 2 splashdown was the U.S. Navy ship USS John P. Murtha.
The Artemis 2 crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Orion "Integrity" capsule underwent a 6-minute communication blackout upon entering the atmosphere.
The Orion "Integrity" capsule deployed parachutes to slow down to a safe landing speed.
